modules.name: Ground-floor activation and frontage composition
modules.design_question: How much of the street frontage is active, transparent, finely grained and sheltered, and how much is lost to blank wall, loading and parking access?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days; the edge-annotation UI (per-facade category, glazing, entrances) is the main cost.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: ground-storey volumes (mesh, z from 0 to first-floor underside) with a program tag per volume
Layer0.ProgramTags: office | residential | hotel | retail | cultural_civic | public | amenity | mechanical | core
SiteContext.StreetEdges (from SITE packet): polylines typed arterial | retail_high_street | lane | mid_block | transit_plaza

EdgeAnnotations (new Layer 0+ attribute, user-drawn): per facade segment category (active | semi_active | passive | blank | service), glazing ratio, entrance points, service/egress doors, canopy geometry
Optional: neighbouring frontages for continuity at corners
outputs: FrontageSegments: GeoJSON FeatureCollection<LineString> {street_type, category, length_m, glazing_ratio, entrances_n}
ActiveFrontagePct: number per street edge
Entrances: Point[] {use, width_m} (consumed by P06-M04 and P06-M05)
BlankRunMax_m, ServiceFrontagePct, WeatherProtectionCoveragePct: numbers per street edge
GroundFloorChecks: Check[] {clause_id, source_id, status, value} (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES boards)

parameters.name: Active-use share of street frontage
parameters.relationship: More retail, cafe, civic or lobby frontage on streets, corners and plazas -> more activity and visibility; but less frontage for cores, loading and back-of-house, which must be relocated to lanes or below grade.

parameters.name: Entrance spacing
parameters.relationship: Smaller spacing (more doors) -> finer grain and more eyes on the street; each extra door uses frontage and adds tenancies. CDDG describes about 8-12 m between entrances on non-residential active facades.

parameters.name: Unit (storefront) frontage width
parameters.relationship: Narrower units -> more varied tenants and a finer rhythm but less efficient anchors; the CDDG expects 7.6-15.3 m with large uses designed to be demisable later.

parameters.name: Ground-floor glazing ratio
parameters.relationship: Higher transparent share of the ground-floor band -> stronger visual permeability and passive surveillance; but more glare and heat gain and less wall for display or back-of-house. CDDG says 'most' of the facade, with no percentage.

parameters.name: Blank-wall run length
parameters.relationship: Longer uninterrupted blank wall, grille or egress-door run -> fewer reasons to stop and lower perceived safety; driven by cores, substations, loading and parkade doors placed on streets.

parameters.name: Vehicle crossings and service-door frontage
parameters.relationship: Each driveway or loading door on a street replaces active frontage and adds pedestrian-vehicle conflict; moving access to the lane removes both. Vancouver policy is to minimise width and number of driveways across sidewalks.

parameters.name: Weather protection depth, height and continuity
parameters.relationship: Deeper, more continuous canopies at 3.0-4.5 m height -> longer rain-sheltered walking and waiting in a wet climate; but they can block daylight and sky view and conflict with street trees.

parameters.name: Ground-storey floor-to-floor height
parameters.relationship: 4.6-6.1 m storeys -> flexible, tall transparent shopfront bands and mezzanines; higher ground storeys raise podium height and construction cost.

parameters.name: Street type (retail high street, arterial, lane, mid-block)
parameters.relationship: Street type sets how strict the active-frontage target should be: continuous on the retail high street, mixed on the arterial, service tolerated on lanes. Designated retail-continuity streets come from the Downtown ODP map, not opened.

metrics.name: Entrance spacing on non-residential active facades
metrics.good: About 8-12 m between entrances (roughly 8-13 entrances per 100 m).
metrics.bad: Gaps above 12 m flagged amber; guideline says 'typically', so it is discretionary, not pass/fail.
metrics.basis: City-wide Design and Development Guidelines (CDDG) S3.1.1a, draft Appendix A as presented to Council 28 Jul 2026. Per-100 m conversion is ours.
metrics.method: Order entrance points along each street edge; compute gaps; report median, max and entrances per 100 m.

metrics.name: Fine-grain unit frontage width
metrics.good: Ground-level fine-grain active units generally 7.6-15.3 m wide.
metrics.bad: Units wider than 15.3 m that are not designed to be demisable; major anchors are better placed below or above grade.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.7.2 and G2.7.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Measure distance between demising lines or tagged unit boundaries along the facade.

metrics.name: Active frontage share by street type
metrics.good: Retail high street at least 90%; arterial and other streets at least 70%; lanes no minimum (editable presets).
metrics.bad: Below 50% on a retail high street or arterial.
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.6.1 only says to locate active uses on fronting streets, corners, open spaces and mid-block links; no percentage exists. Downtown ODP retail-continuity requirement (S15) is not numerically quoted and its street map was not opened.
metrics.method: Length of active segments divided by total street-facing frontage length, per street type.

metrics.name: Ground-floor transparency ratio
metrics.good: At least 60% glazed in the band from grade to the lower of second-floor underside or canopy soffit (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 40% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.1.1b requires transparent glazing across 'most' of the ground-floor facade but gives no number. The 60% figure is a placeholder; Seattle and San Francisco codes are possible analogues but were not opened.
metrics.method: Glazed area divided by facade area in the band; use modelled openings or the annotated ratio.

metrics.name: Longest blank or opaque run
metrics.good: No run longer than about 10 m (about one entrance spacing, editable).
metrics.bad: Run longer than 15 m (editable).
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.1.2 and G2.15.3 say to limit or avoid blank walls, grilles, secondary egress doors and opaque glazing along streets, but set no length.
metrics.method: Maximum consecutive length of blank, service or passive segments along a street edge.

metrics.name: Weather-protection geometry
metrics.good: Mounting height 3.0-4.5 m; depth-to-height ratio about 0.4-0.7; depth at least 1.5 m in most mixed-use contexts.
metrics.bad: Outside these ranges, or missing over active frontages, transit and entries.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.2.1 and S3.2.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Sample canopy depth and underside height every 2 m along active frontage; compute ratio.

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage of active frontage
metrics.good: Generally continuous along non-residential active frontages, at least 90% of length (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% of length (preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG G3.2.1 asks for generally continuous protection, particularly where pedestrian activity is high; the percentages are placeholders.
metrics.method: Canopy length divided by active frontage length.

metrics.name: Vehicle access and service frontage on streets
metrics.good: Vehicle access from the lane; no driveway or loading door on retail high street or arterial frontage where lane access exists.
metrics.bad: Any street-side crossing where lane access is feasible; count and width reported.
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.10.1 (access from lane, away from streets) and Transportation 2040 W 1.1.6 (minimise width and number of driveways across sidewalks). No numeric cap exists.
metrics.method: Count vehicle crossings and sum service-door lengths per street edge.

metrics.name: Active-storey floor-to-floor height
metrics.good: 4.6-6.1 m for active-use storeys.
metrics.bad: Below 4.6 m for retail, or above 6.1 m without a mezzanine rationale.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.7.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Read storey heights of tagged active volumes.

modules.method: 1) Offset each ground-storey footprint edge facing a street, mid-block link or plaza and split it at entrances, demising lines and tag changes. 2) Classify each segment as active, semi-active, passive, blank or service from tags, glazing and entrances. 3) Sum lengths by street type; compute entrances per 100 m, gap distribution, unit widths and longest blank run. 4) Glazing ratio equals glazed area over facade area between grade and the lower of second-floor underside and canopy soffit. 5) Sample canopy mounting height and depth along the frontage. 6) Count vehicle crossings and service-door lengths. 7) Look up thresholds in a JSON table where every row carries source id and status (verified, team assumption, unverified). Recompute on any geometry or tag change.
visualization: Plan view: each street edge offset 1 m outward and drawn as a thick polyline coloured by category (active green, semi-active teal, passive amber, blank grey with hatch, service purple), entrances as triangles, 10 m tick marks; colour-blind-safe palette plus pattern fills.
Unrolled elevation strip per street (x = length in m, y = grade to second floor) with glazing percentage as a filled line and unit-width bars drawn against the 7.6-15.3 m band.
Bar chart of active percentage per street with the preset target line; one pass/fail badge per clause linking to the CDDG clause and source id.
Team-assumption metrics drawn with a dashed outline and an editable-threshold chip; any later-disproved threshold is shown in the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour.
modules.human_judgment: Whether a use is genuinely active (tenant, opening hours, display), perceived safety and character of the edge, material quality at touch distance, and whether a justified breach (for example a civic anchor with a long frontage) is better than the rule. The jury may reward justified breaches.
modules.limits: Layer 0 holds no facade openings, so glazing and entrances need annotation or modelled windows. Activity is inferred from tags, not from occupancy. Retail-continuity designations for the VTC streets are unknown because the site is hypothetical. CDDG figures are guidelines ('typically', 'generally'), not by-law limits.

modules.name: Streetwall, podium setbacks and street enclosure
modules.design_question: Do podium height, tower step-back, tower separation and floorplate give a street room of comfortable proportion and keep sky and light at the pedestrian level?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days; section sampling and lookup tables are simple, context towers need SITE data.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: per-storey footprints and storey heights, with podium/tower split derived from first step-back
SiteContext.StreetEdges with right-of-way (ROW) width between building lines, including sidewalks
SiteContext.Buildings: existing and approved neighbouring towers (from SITE packet)
SiteContext.NorthAngle: rotation of true north relative to the street grid
Layer0.ProgramTags per storey (to split tower floorplates into employment, hotel and residential portions)
outputs: StreetSections: {street_id, station_m, podium_h_m, row_w_m, hw_ratio, step_back_m, sky_view_factor}[]
PodiumBandCheck: {street_id, allowed_min_m, allowed_max_m, actual_m, status}
TowerChecks: {floorplate_avg_m2, max_dimension_m, separation_to_neighbour_m, required_m, status}[]
StreetwallContinuityPct per street edge
SkyPlots: stereographic sky maps at sampled eye points (consumed by CLIM and P06-M08)

parameters.name: Podium (streetwall) height
parameters.relationship: Taller podium on a given street -> higher height-to-width ratio, stronger enclosure and less visible sky at the sidewalk (geometry). The CDDG caps podium height by street width so enclosure stays near a fixed band.

parameters.name: Street right-of-way width (building line to building line)
parameters.relationship: Wider street (sidewalks included) -> taller podium allowed for the same enclosure; Downtown mixed-use and non-residential podiums step from about 15.2 m on narrow streets to 18.3-23.0 m above 30.5 m wide.

parameters.name: Tower step-back above podium
parameters.relationship: Setback above the podium makes the base read as the street wall and hides tower mass from the sidewalk; a planar change of 1.5-3.0 m is the smallest that reads as a volumetric break.

parameters.name: Massing variation interval along the street
parameters.relationship: Variation every 25-46 m breaks long monolithic walls into a human-scale rhythm; longer unbroken runs read as monolithic.

parameters.name: Tower floorplate area and dimension
parameters.relationship: Larger floorplate -> wider tower, wider shadow and less sky from the street (geometry). CDDG gives average maxima by use and a 29.0 m dimension limit for residential towers.

parameters.name: Tower separation
parameters.relationship: More separation between towers -> more daylight, privacy and sky reaching the public realm. Minimum 15.2 m employment-employment up to 24.4 m residential-residential; employment and hotel towers in the CBD may reduce it if light in the public realm is protected.

parameters.name: Corner setbacks at north-south street corners
parameters.relationship: Setting massing back at north-south street corners opens street-end mountain views; the downtown grid is rotated, so 'north-south' must be taken from the street grid, not true north.

parameters.name: Massing over open space
parameters.relationship: Overhead massing over a POPS removes that area from the POPS count and reduces sun and sky; elsewhere a clear height of 12-18 m is expected under overhanging mass.

metrics.name: Podium height versus street width (Downtown tower podiums)
metrics.good: Podium within the band for its street: up to 15.2 m for streets up to 27.5 m wide; 15.2-18.3 m up to 30.5 m; 18.3-23.0 m above 30.5 m. Residential towers: podium maximum 18.3 m Downtown (21.3 m in listed exceptions).
metrics.bad: Podium above the band for its street width; needs a written justification.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 2.2b and S2.2.6-S2.2.8 (draft Appendix A). Table 2.2b was reconstructed from the PDF text layout, so recheck against the final posted CDDG.
metrics.method: Look up ROW width, compare podium height from the first step-back.

metrics.name: Implied podium height-to-width ratio
metrics.good: About 0.6-0.75 for tower podiums (derived from Table 2.2b); about 1:1 to 1:1.1 for low-rise residential streetwalls.
metrics.bad: Above the band for the street type.
metrics.basis: Derived from CDDG Table 2.2b (15.2/24.4, 18.3/30.5, 23.0/30.5) and S2.2.2. The ratio is our calculation, not a quoted rule.
metrics.method: Podium height divided by face-to-face ROW width, sampled every 5 m along the street.

metrics.name: Tower step-back above podium
metrics.good: A massing setback above the podium, with at least about 1.5-3.0 m planar change.
metrics.bad: Tower faces flush with the podium plane on a street where a defined streetwall is wanted.
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.2.2 and design tip on minimum planar change (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Horizontal offset between podium face and first tower storey face.

metrics.name: Average tower floorplate
metrics.good: Employment and hotel towers about 930-1,395 m2; residential tall towers up to 746 m2; very tall residential towers 930-1,115 m2.
metrics.bad: Above the maximum; reviewed case by case.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 2.3 and S2.3.3. Tall = above about 90 m, very tall = above about 150 m (glossary).
metrics.method: Slice the mesh at every tower storey and average gross floor area by use portion.

metrics.name: Tower separation
metrics.good: At or above Table 1.5: employment-employment 15.2 m, employment-hotel 15.2 m, employment-residential 18.3 m, residential-residential 24.4 m.
metrics.bad: Below the table value, unless the CBD employment/hotel exception applies and light loss in the public realm is minimised.
metrics.basis: CDDG Table 1.5 and S1.5.1-S1.5.3 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Minimum horizontal distance between facing tower storeys, own tower to neighbour towers, per storey.

metrics.name: Massing variation interval
metrics.good: Variation in massing about every 25.0-45.7 m of frontage.
metrics.bad: Unbroken facade longer than 45.7 m.
metrics.basis: CDDG S2.2.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Detect plane changes of at least 1.5 m along the street face and measure spacing.

metrics.name: Streetwall continuity
metrics.good: At least 80% of block-face length within 1 m of the build-to line on the retail high street (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% (preset).
metrics.basis: CDDG G2.2.1 says maintain continuity where a continuous streetwall is desired but gives no percentage.
metrics.method: Length of facade within 1 m of the street line at 1.6 m and 12 m heights divided by block-face length.

metrics.name: Sky view factor at sidewalk and street centre
metrics.good: Reported as a change from the by-right or existing baseline; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: No Vancouver threshold found; literature thresholds (Ewing and Handy) were not opened.
metrics.method: Cast 145 hemispherical (Tregenza) rays from 1.6 m eye height and report open-sky fraction.

modules.method: For every street edge, cut perpendicular sections every 5 m. At each section ray-cast left and right from a 1.6 m eye point to get facing building heights, face-to-face width, podium height (height at first step-back of at least 1.5 m) and step-back distance. Compute height-to-width ratio and compare podium height with the Table 2.2b band for the measured ROW width. Sample sky view factor with 145 hemisphere rays. Slice the mesh at each storey above the podium to get floorplate area, maximum dimension and tower footprint; measure minimum facade-to-facade distance to each neighbouring tower and look up the required separation by use pair. Measure streetwall continuity by intersecting facade footprints with a 2 m buffer of the building line. All thresholds come from versioned lookup tables carrying source ids.
visualization: Street cross-section drawing per frontage: podium and tower profile, eye-height cone, shaded allowed-podium band for that ROW, and the measured height-to-width ratio labelled.
Plan: each street segment coloured by podium status (inside band green, above band red, no podium grey) with tower footprints and separation lines labelled in metres against required values.
Stereographic sky plot at chosen eye points with percentage of open sky and baseline comparison.
Pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clause numbers; table-reconstruction caveat shown beside Table 2.2b results.
modules.human_judgment: Perceived enclosure and scale in context, rhythm and proportion of the base, response to heritage or neighbours, skyline and crown quality, and any justified departure from the guideline bands.
modules.limits: Vancouver Table 2.2b and Table 1.5 are discretionary guidelines in draft Appendix A, text-reconstructed. Table 2.2a (low-rise streetwall, east-west versus north-south) does not map cleanly onto the rotated downtown grid. Sky view factor and wind downwash have no sourced pass level here.

modules.name: Public open space: quantity, quality, sun, wind link and access
modules.design_question: Is there enough contiguous public open space, is it sunny, comfortable, furnished and open to everyone, and does the tower's shadow protect neighbouring public spaces?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days; area and POPS checks about 2, sun mapping about 4 if the CLIM shadow engine is reused.
inputs: Layer0.Massing and SiteBoundary
GroundPlane polygons tagged POPS | mid_block | plaza | transit_plaza | retail_patio | park_dedication | private
Seating objects (points or lines with type and back flag), tree canopy polygons
CLIM: shadow engine output for 22 September, 10:00-16:00 local Pacific time in 15-minute steps (own, existing and approved context)
CLIM: pedestrian wind comfort class grid at 1.5 m (if available)
AccessAttributes per space: free | ticketed, opening hours, SRW (statutory right-of-way) yes/no
SiteContext.ProtectedSpaces: Table 1 parks, school sites, plazas, Davie/Robson north sidewalks (from SITE packet)
outputs: PublicOpenSpaceAreas: {type, area_m2, pct_of_site, contiguous, proportion}[]
SunHoursGrid: raster of direct-sun hours (0-6 h) on the ground, 0.5-1.0 m cells
ShadowCoverage: {space_id, existing_pct, added_pct, cumulative_pct, series_per_15min}[]
SeatingSupply: {m_per_100m2, with_backs_pct, types}
OpenSpaceChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES)

parameters.name: Public open space share of site area
parameters.relationship: More public open space -> more room for gathering, trees and sun; but less ground-level building footprint. VTC block is about 11,468 m2, so 10% is about 1,147 m2 and 20% about 2,294 m2.

parameters.name: POPS shape, contiguity and size
parameters.relationship: A contiguous space of about 300 m2 or more with 1:1-1:2 proportions is usable as a neighbourhood space; narrow or fragmented leftovers do not qualify and read as private.

parameters.name: Overhead massing and podium location of the space
parameters.relationship: Mass over a POPS removes it from the POPS count and cuts sun and sky; space on podium or roof without public stairs and lifts also does not count.

parameters.name: Tower height, floorplate and position relative to the space
parameters.relationship: Taller, wider tower to the south or west of a space -> longer, wider shadow -> fewer sunlit hours there (geometry; confirm by simulation). Vancouver tests 10:00-16:00 on 22 September in 15-minute steps.

parameters.name: Wind exposure at seating (from CLIM)
parameters.relationship: Taller towers and open corners tend to raise ground-level wind -> fewer comfortable sitting hours. Higher Buildings Policy says tall buildings should not add adverse microclimate effects; CDDG says site open space away from wind.

parameters.name: Seating quantity and type
parameters.relationship: More seating with backs, in sun and shade, and at corners and mid-block links -> longer stays and wider use by older people; NYC requires 1 linear foot per 30 sq ft of plaza.

parameters.name: Retail patio share of a POPS
parameters.relationship: More private patio inside a POPS -> less space and less perceived publicness; CDDG limits patios to about one third of a POPS.

parameters.name: Access hours and legal tenure (SRW)
parameters.relationship: Longer, unconditional hours and a statutory right-of-way -> the space works as public; early closing or gates reduce use. NYC default is open at all times, with limited closings allowed only by authorisation.

parameters.name: Planting, soil volume and underground setbacks
parameters.relationship: Underground setbacks and slab drops enable in-ground trees, shade and habitat; CDDG asks for tree planting in plazas where contiguous planted areas or setbacks exist.

parameters.name: Transit plaza size
parameters.relationship: Space next to a station entrance sized for waiting and circulation (at least about 6.1 m by 6.1 m) supports transit use; it is not counted as park dedication.

metrics.name: Public open space as share of site area
metrics.good: At least 20% on large or unique sites; at least 10% on mid-sized sites (4,000-8,000 m2); about 10% as POPS on non-residential tower sites with frontage over 60.7 m.
metrics.bad: Below the applicable target; park dedication may be requested instead.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.9.1, S1.9.2, S1.10.2. Whether the VTC block counts as a 'large site' is unresolved because the definition sits in another policy.
metrics.method: Sum areas of tagged public open space meeting the counting rules; divide by site area (11,468 m2 for the VTC block).

metrics.name: POPS geometry and eligibility
metrics.good: Contiguous, proportion 1:1 or 1:2, area about 300 m2 or more, secured by SRW, free of overhead massing; excludes setbacks, engineering SRWs, vehicle space, and podium or roof areas without public stairs and lifts.
metrics.bad: Fragmented, under mass, without SRW or access points.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.11.1 and glossary definition of POPS.
metrics.method: Apply eligibility filters to tagged polygons; compute minimum bounding rectangle aspect.

metrics.name: Direct sun on own public open space
metrics.good: At least 50% of POPS area has 2 or more hours of direct sun on 22 September between 10:00 and 16:00 (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Less than 25% of area reaches 2 hours (editable preset).
metrics.basis: Vancouver sets the assessment window (verified) but no minimum sun for new private-development open space. The 2-hour, 50% test follows the BRE BR 209 practice, which was not opened.
metrics.method: Cast shadows at 25 time steps (10:00-16:00, 15 min); count lit steps per cell; hours equals lit steps times 0.25.

metrics.name: New shadow on protected public spaces
metrics.good: No new shadow on community, neighbourhood or local parks or school sites on 22 September 10:00-16:00; no new shadow on the north sidewalk of Davie Village (10:00-16:00) or Robson Village (10:00-15:00); urban plazas: actively minimise.
metrics.bad: Any added shadow without a shadow rationale statement, solar budget at 15-minute steps and detailed study. Staff note about 5-15% added shadow is typical for high-rises but set no benchmark.
metrics.basis: Solar Access Guidelines for the Downtown Peninsula, redline text in memo RTS 16506 (17 Sep 2025); times amended from PDT to PT on 28 Jul 2026. Shadow coverage % = total shadow area over 25 steps / (space area x 25).
metrics.method: Compute existing, added and cumulative shadow area per 15-minute step and the coverage formula for each Table 1 space.

metrics.name: Seating supply
metrics.good: At least 1 linear foot per 30 sq ft of plaza (about 1 m per 9.1 m2), at least two seating types, at least 50% with backs; moveable seating on plazas over 10,000 sq ft; seating at street corners and mid-block links.
metrics.bad: Less than half of the NYC quantity, or no seating at corners and links.
metrics.basis: NYC Zoning Resolution 37-741 is an external benchmark, not a Vancouver rule; CDDG G3.4.2 supports seating at corners and mid-block connections.
metrics.method: Sum linear seating metres by type; divide by plaza area; count backs.

metrics.name: Wind comfort at seating
metrics.good: Sitting or standing comfort class over at least 75% of seating area (editable preset, class definitions come from CLIM).
metrics.bad: Strolling class or worse at seating.
metrics.basis: No wind criterion with a Vancouver source was opened; wind class thresholds belong to the CLIM packet. The 75% figure is a placeholder.
metrics.method: Intersect CLIM comfort-class grid with seating polygons.

metrics.name: Access hours and tenure
metrics.good: Public open space secured by SRW and open at least from 7:00 to 22:00 in summer and 7:00 to 20:00 in winter; mid-block links 24 hours (preset).
metrics.bad: Hours shorter than the NYC allowed-closing schedule, ticketed entry, or no SRW.
metrics.basis: CDDG requires SRWs for POPS and mid-block links but states no hours. Hours come from the NYC authorised-closing schedule (external benchmark).
metrics.method: Read access attributes; compare to the schedule.

metrics.name: Retail patio share of POPS
metrics.good: Patios no more than about one third of the POPS; signage states public use.
metrics.bad: Above one third, or no public-use signage.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.6.1 and S3.6.2.
metrics.method: Patio area divided by POPS area.

metrics.name: Transit plaza minimum size
metrics.good: At least about 6.1 m by 6.1 m beside a station entrance.
metrics.bad: Smaller, or counted toward park dedication.
metrics.basis: CDDG S4.4.1 and G1.9.1.
metrics.method: Largest inscribed rectangle in the plaza polygon.

modules.method: Tag ground-plane polygons; apply the CDDG counting rules (remove setbacks, engineering SRWs, vehicle areas, areas under mass, elevated areas without public stairs or lifts) to get public open space area and share of site. Check contiguity and proportion with minimum rotated rectangles. For sun, compute solar position for 22 September at 15-minute steps from 10:00 to 16:00 local Pacific time at the site latitude, cast shadows of own, existing and approved massing onto a ground grid, and store lit-step counts. Report hours per cell, share of area with at least 2 hours, and shadow coverage percentage per protected space using the City formula. Intersect CLIM wind class grid with seating. Sum seating metres by type. Compare each result with the threshold table.
visualization: Ground-plane false-colour mesh of direct-sun hours with a 0-6 h legend, a bold contour at 2 h, POPS outlines hatched, seating points on top, and a 15-minute time scrubber from 10:00 to 16:00.
Protected-space panel: stacked area chart of existing and added shadow percent against time, with the City coverage percentage printed.
Horizontal bars of public open space percent against the 10% and 20% target lines, each with a source badge.
Pass/fail badge list linked to CDDG clauses; team-assumption rows dashed and editable.
modules.human_judgment: Programming and stewardship, who the space feels welcome to, perceived safety, relation to Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh place-making, choice between park dedication and POPS (decided by City and Park Board), and whether a shadow trade-off is justified by public benefit.
modules.limits: Sun is computed with clear-sky geometry only; Vancouver is often overcast in fall. Trees and small structures are ignored, as in the City baseline. Wind comfort and shadow engines belong to the CLIM packet. The CDDG space targets are 'target' guidelines; the 20% versus 10% POPS overlap is unresolved.

modules.name: Permeability, mid-block connections and block structure
modules.design_question: Does the block give direct, legible, step-free-ready public routes through it, especially between the transit station, the high street and the arterial?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days; the network graph and width checks are simple, route directness needs the station entrance location.
inputs: SiteBoundary and SiteContext.StreetNetwork (streets, lanes, existing mid-block links) from OSM or City open data
Layer0.Massing and ground-plane passage polylines with clear width, open-to-sky flag, hours and SRW flag
SiteContext.TransitEntrances: existing station entrance and the required below-grade secondary entrance (from MOBI packet or site plan)
Destinations: retail high street, arterial crossings, parks, plazas (from SITE packet)
outputs: WalkGraph: NetworkX graph {nodes: entrances, junctions; edges: length_m, clear_width_m, open_to_sky, hours}
ConnectionChecks: {connection_id, required, clear_width_m, min_required_m, status}[]
DirectnessTable: {from, to, network_m, straight_m, prd}[] (PRD = pedestrian route directness)
Isochrones: polygons for 2-, 5- and 10-minute walks from the station entrance
RouteGraph for P06-M05 (flows) and P06-M06 (step-free routing)

parameters.name: Number and location of mid-block connections
parameters.relationship: More public through-routes -> shorter walks and more route choice, and more active edges; each link removes buildable area. CDDG requires one where the site is adjacent to or includes a station entrance.

parameters.name: Connection width (building face to building face)
parameters.relationship: Wider links feel safer and allow daylight and active edges but cost site area; CDDG ranges are 4.5 m (half share), 5.4 m non-residential, 7.3 m voluntary and 9.1 m large sites, with a 2.4 m clear path.

parameters.name: Open to sky versus covered breezeway
parameters.relationship: Covered links need height-to-width of at least 2:1, active edges, a direct line and public hours or they read as tunnels; open-to-sky links are the default.

parameters.name: Alignment with desire lines and destinations
parameters.relationship: Links that join the station, parks and high street pick up existing pedestrian flows; links to nowhere stay empty and unsafe.

parameters.name: Route directness (network over straight-line distance)
parameters.relationship: Detours of the through-route above straight-line distance raise walking time and reduce use; connected street networks are positively associated with physical activity in a meta-analysis (mainly children).

parameters.name: Hours of public access of each link
parameters.relationship: Links closed outside building hours cut the network at night; breezeways may be limited to building hours by the CDDG, mid-block links secured by SRW are public.

parameters.name: Grade separation of the transit link
parameters.relationship: A below-grade secondary entrance takes crowds off the surface but needs a lift, stairs, active uses and a visual link to the concourse to stay legible.

metrics.name: Mid-block connection required by station adjacency
metrics.good: At least one public connection provided where the site includes or adjoins a station entrance.
metrics.bad: No connection although the trigger applies.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.1b and G1.12.2 (draft Appendix A). The VTC brief requires a secondary transit entrance, so the trigger applies.
metrics.method: Check presence and endpoints of connections against station entrance location.

metrics.name: Connection width
metrics.good: Building face to building face at least 9.1 m on large sites or identified links; at least 5.4 m in non-residential contexts; 4.5 m from face to shared line if neighbour delivers the other half; 7.3 m when voluntary; clear path at least 2.4 m.
metrics.bad: Narrower than the applicable value.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.2 and S3.8.1; variations allowed by G1.12.1.
metrics.method: Minimum distance between facing facades along the link centreline.

metrics.name: Open to sky or compliant breezeway
metrics.good: Primarily open to sky; a breezeway only if height-to-width at least 2:1, lined with active uses, direct and public, open during building hours.
metrics.bad: Enclosed passage not meeting these tests.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.4 and S2.2.10.
metrics.method: Compute roofed share and height-to-width of each link.

metrics.name: Route directness between key pairs
metrics.good: At most 1.25 for station to high street, and across-block pairs (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Above 1.5 (editable preset).
metrics.basis: No sourced Vancouver or other threshold was opened. Vancouver Transportation 2040 notes the grid gives direct walking routes.
metrics.method: Shortest path length on the walk graph divided by straight-line distance.

metrics.name: Longest stretch of block perimeter without a public through-route
metrics.good: At most about 100 m (editable preset); the VTC long side is 144.8 m, so one link near the middle gives about 72 m.
metrics.bad: Above 150 m (editable preset).
metrics.basis: No sourced block-length rule was found for Vancouver; this is a starting value.
metrics.method: Distance between consecutive public openings along the block perimeter.

metrics.name: Public access tenure of required links
metrics.good: Required links secured by SRW and open to the public.
metrics.bad: No SRW or access limited to a private operator's hours.
metrics.basis: CDDG S1.12.3 requires an SRW; 24-hour opening is not stated.
metrics.method: Read SRW flag and hours attribute.

metrics.name: Street intersection density (context scale)
metrics.good: Reported only; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: Street intersection density is positively associated with physical activity in a systematic review (mainly children); thresholds such as LEED ND values were not opened.
metrics.method: OSMnx intersections within 800 m of the site divided by area.

modules.method: Build a walk graph from the street network, lanes, sidewalks, mid-block links and building passages, with each edge carrying length, clear width, open-to-sky flag and hours. Check each connection against width and sky-openness tables. Compute shortest paths between station entrance(s), high-street midpoint, arterial crossings and each public entrance from P06-M01, then divide by straight-line distance to get route directness. Compute 2-, 5- and 10-minute walk areas from the station entrance at a preset walking speed. Compute longest uninterrupted perimeter stretch without a public through-route. Optionally compute context intersection density and visual integration with space-syntax tools for comparison.
visualization: Plan with the walk graph drawn over the block: edges coloured by clear width (below 2.4 m red, 2.4-4.5 m amber, 4.5 m and over green), open-to-sky edges solid and covered edges dashed.
Isochrone rings (2, 5, 10 minutes) from the station entrance, shaded by time, with labelled route directness for the three key pairs.
Perimeter ruler around the block marking public openings and the longest gap.
Pass/fail badge list linked to CDDG clauses; team-assumption rows editable.
modules.human_judgment: Legibility and sightlines, whether the link feels public rather than private, night-time safety, wayfinding including Indigenous place names, and negotiation with TransLink and the neighbouring site for the secondary station entrance.
modules.limits: Pure geometry: it does not model crowding, weather or pedestrian choice. Route directness and block-gap thresholds are presets without a source. Walking speed is a preset. The below-grade link must be drawn by the user; Layer 0 may not include it.

modules.name: Sidewalk capacity and pedestrian level of service
modules.design_question: At peak times, are the sidewalks and corners around the block wide enough for comfortable walking once furniture, queues and station flows are counted?
modules.effort: About 4-6 person-days for static footway comfort; agent-based simulation (roadmap) adds about 8-10 days.
inputs: StreetSections: sidewalk total width, building edge, trees, furniture, bike racks, canopy posts (SITE and user sections)
P06-M01 Entrances and program GFA by use from Layer 0
MOBI: station and bus-stop flows (persons per peak hour) at the transit entrances
PedestrianDemandPreset: person trips per 100 m2 GFA by use, peak-hour share, walk share (editable team assumptions)
Street area type: high street | office and retail | residential | tourist | transport interchange
outputs: FootwayComfort: {segment_id, flow_ppmm, pcl_class, clear_width_m, required_width_m}[]
WidthBudget: stacked widths building buffer + active zone + clear + furniture + kerb buffer
CornerQueueAreas: polygons with area per person
PCLChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08)

parameters.name: Peak-hour pedestrian flow
parameters.relationship: More office, retail and hotel floor area, and closer transit, -> higher peak flows on adjacent sidewalks. Rates per m2 are team assumptions (no sourced Vancouver generation rates found).

parameters.name: Effective clear width
parameters.relationship: Total width minus 0.2 m building and kerb buffers and furniture buffers -> flow per metre of effective width rises as obstacles are added; one bench or tree pit can drop comfort a class.

parameters.name: Flow per metre of width (ppmm)
parameters.relationship: Pedestrians per minute per metre of effective width: higher values mean more bumping and slower walking, from under 3 ppmm (A+) to over 35 ppmm (E).

parameters.name: Area type and tolerance
parameters.relationship: Transport interchanges and tourist areas tolerate less crowding than residential streets; level B+ is the recommended minimum everywhere.

parameters.name: Static activity (queues, window shoppers, cafe seating)
parameters.relationship: People standing or sitting use width that walkers cannot; patios and displays can reduce clearway below 2.4 m if not allowed for in the boulevard.

parameters.name: Building setback or SRW widening
parameters.relationship: Setting the building back adds clear width at no street cost; commercial corridors have been asked for at least 5.5 m from back of curb (1.0 m back boulevard, 3.0 m clear, 1.5 m front boulevard).

parameters.name: Transit arrival surges
parameters.relationship: Train arrivals deliver short, high peaks at station entrances; use the average-of-maximum activity level for interchange areas rather than the hourly mean.

metrics.name: Pedestrian Comfort Level (PCL) at peak flow
metrics.good: PCL B+ or better, which is 11 ppmm or fewer (B+ is 9-11 ppmm).
metrics.bad: PCL C+ or worse (18 ppmm and above); D (27-35 ppmm) and E (over 35 ppmm) are very uncomfortable; even with compensation such as cafe seating, never below C+.
metrics.basis: TfL Pedestrian Comfort Guidance for London, Figure 8 and area-type guidance (2010). London research, not Vancouver calibrated.
metrics.method: ppmm = peak-period flow per minute divided by effective clear width; map to class table.

metrics.name: Clear sidewalk width, Vancouver standard
metrics.good: Commercial and mixed-use streets: at least 3.0 m clear, wider by volume; downtown clearways of 3.0-5.0 m exist; 4.0 m for new high-volume corridors.
metrics.bad: Below 2.4 m (the constrained minimum) or below 3.0 m on commercial streets without City Engineer agreement.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 and Table 8-3.
metrics.method: Read clear width from the section after removing furniture and patio encroachment.

metrics.name: Pedestrian realm depth from back of curb
metrics.good: About 5.5 m (1.0 m back boulevard + 3.0 m clear + 1.5 m front boulevard) on commercial corridors.
metrics.bad: Below that without a City Engineer-approved reason.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 (historic request for redevelopment projects).
metrics.method: Measure back of curb to property line plus SRW.

metrics.name: Recommended total footway width by flow class
metrics.good: Under 600 pph: 2.9 m; 600-1,200 pph: 4.2 m; over 1,200 pph: 5.3 m total (3.3 m if no furniture).
metrics.bad: Below the recommended width for the flow class.
metrics.basis: TfL guidance, Appendix B.
metrics.method: Classify segment flow; compare total width.

metrics.name: Minimum pedestrian way and obstacle gaps
metrics.good: Footway at least 2.0 m (1.5 m acceptable under constraint); gaps at obstacles at least 1.0 m and no longer than 6 m; furniture at least 1.0 m from vehicle crossings and entrances.
metrics.bad: Below these.
metrics.basis: UK DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2 (external); City of Vancouver EDM clearances (1.0 m from vehicle crossings and entrances).
metrics.method: Scan sections for obstacle gaps.

metrics.name: Legacy Fruin level of service cross-check
metrics.good: Level C or better by area per pedestrian (values to be confirmed).
metrics.bad: Level E or F.
metrics.basis: Fruin 1971 and Highway Capacity Manual thresholds were recalled, not opened. TfL guidance says Fruin only assesses crowding, not comfort.
metrics.method: Area per pedestrian from density; map to Fruin classes.

metrics.name: Peak pedestrian generation assumptions
metrics.good: Editable presets by use, flagged as assumptions.
metrics.bad: Any figure without a source or label.
metrics.basis: No sourced Vancouver trip generation rates were found. Transportation 2040 target of two-thirds of trips on foot, bike or transit by 2040 is context only.
metrics.method: GFA by use times rate times peak-hour share times walk share.

modules.method: For each sidewalk segment adjacent to the site, build the width budget from the street section: total width minus 0.2 m building buffer, 0.2 m kerb buffer and buffers around trees, poles, benches, racks and canopy posts, as in the TfL method. Estimate peak flow by distributing person-trips from each entrance (P06-M01) and station entrance flows (MOBI) onto adjacent segments using shortest paths on the walk graph from P06-M04, with a preset peak-hour share. Convert flow to ppmm and map to the PCL class table with the area type's tolerance. Report required width for B+ and the shortfall. Check Vancouver clear-width and realm-depth standards. Optionally run an agent-based simulation and analyse density and flow from trajectories.
visualization: Plan view: each sidewalk segment drawn as a ribbon coloured by PCL class (11-class sequential-to-diverging scale from A+ blue to E dark red) with a ppmm legend.
Cross-section bars per segment: building buffer, active zone, clear width, furniture, kerb buffer, with a marker at the width needed for B+.
Line chart of ppmm against hour of day for each segment, with the B+ line and the C+ line drawn.
Pass/fail badges linked to TfL and EDM clauses; assumption presets shown dashed.
modules.human_judgment: Peak scenario choice (event days, train arrival waves), how to trade clear width against trees, patios and seating, perceived crowding by older people and children, and seasonal or weather effects.
modules.limits: TfL comfort levels come from London footway studies; Vancouver conditions differ. Flow is estimated from assumption presets, not counts. Cyclists, e-scooters and vehicle crossings are not modelled in the static check. Fruin values are unverified.

modules.name: Inclusive and accessible design at grade
modules.design_question: Can everyone, including wheelchair users, people with low vision and older people, reach and use every public entrance, space and the station link at grade without barriers?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days; slope mapping and rest-spacing checks are simple, door and entrance data need annotation.
inputs: Terrain: DEM or spot elevations for the site and surrounding streets (SITE packet)
Layer0 ground slab levels, entrances with threshold heights, stairs, ramps and lifts (tagged objects)
P06-M04 RouteGraph and clear widths
Seating points from P06-M03; crossing and curb-ramp points
Manual fields: door clear width, automatic openers, tactile surfaces, accessible washrooms
outputs: SlopeMap: raster of running slope (%) and crossfall (%)
StepFreeRoutes: {from_entrance, to_target, step_free, max_slope, max_gap_to_rest_m}[]
RestCoverage: polygons within 50 m, 100 m and 150 m of seating
AccessChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES)

parameters.name: Running slope of public routes
parameters.relationship: Steeper slope -> more effort and need to rest; 5% (1:20) is the target, anything steeper is a ramp, and 1:12 is the absolute maximum for short runs.

parameters.name: Crossfall
parameters.relationship: Crossfall drains water but makes wheelchairs drift and challenges balance; Vancouver designs 2% (1-4% range), UK guidance prefers 1-2% with 1 in 40 as the maximum.

parameters.name: Level change between sidewalk and slab
parameters.relationship: Bigger grade differences force stairs, ramps or lifts; CDDG says integrate them in the building envelope and keep a visual and physical connection to the public realm.

parameters.name: Clear path width
parameters.relationship: At least 2.0 m lets two wheelchairs pass; 1.5 m lets a wheelchair and a walker pass; 1.0 m at obstacles for no more than 6 m.

parameters.name: Spacing of seats and rest spots
parameters.relationship: Closer rests let more people complete a walk: Vancouver gives 150 m for wheelchair and visually impaired users, 100 m for mobility impaired without a stick, 50 m for stick users; UK guidance says seats at 50 m or closer in busy areas.

parameters.name: Landings on slopes
parameters.relationship: Level landings at least every 0.5 m of rise, as long as the ramp is wide, give rest points and allow passing.

parameters.name: Headroom under canopies, stairs and soffits
parameters.relationship: Headroom of at least 2.3 m prevents head strikes by people with low vision; undersides of stairs need a barrier below that height.

parameters.name: Tactile surfaces at flush crossings
parameters.relationship: Flush crossings lack a curb cue; Vancouver requires truncated domes where grade break is under 5%, so layout must leave room for paired bracketing.

parameters.name: Governing building code and standards
parameters.relationship: BC Building Code does not apply in Vancouver; the Vancouver Building By-law and CSA B651 govern barrier-free entrances, ramps and doors. Numeric requirements were not opened.

metrics.name: Running slope of public paths
metrics.good: At most 5% (1:20) where achievable.
metrics.bad: Above 8.3% (1:12), the absolute ramp maximum; between 5% and 8.3% is a ramp needing landings and handrails.
metrics.basis: Engineering Design Manual 2026 (5% maximum running slope where achievable); DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.3 (1:20; 1:12 absolute maximum).
metrics.method: Slope from DEM or pathway profile along each route segment.

metrics.name: Crossfall
metrics.good: 1-2% (about 1 in 50).
metrics.bad: Above 2.5% (1 in 40) per UK guidance; Vancouver allows up to 4% on constrained sites, so show amber between 2.5 and 4%.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 8.4.3.3 and DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.3; the two sources differ at the upper end.
metrics.method: Cross slope across the sidewalk from the section.

metrics.name: Clear width of public routes
metrics.good: At least 3.0 m on commercial streets; at least 2.4 m on mid-block links; 2.0 m desirable for any footway.
metrics.bad: Below 1.5 m anywhere, or below 1.0 m at obstacles longer than 6 m.
metrics.basis: EDM Table 8-3; CDDG S3.8.1; DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2.
metrics.method: Minimum clear width per route segment from P06-M04.

metrics.name: Rest spacing along public routes
metrics.good: A seat or rest spot at most 50 m apart along busy routes; 100-150 m acceptable for other groups.
metrics.bad: Gaps over 150 m.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 Table 8-2 (research from the late 1980s) and DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.5 (50 m).
metrics.method: Distance along routes between seating nodes; compare to groups in Table 8-2.

metrics.name: Landings and headroom
metrics.good: Landing for each 0.5 m of rise; headroom at least 2.3 m.
metrics.bad: Longer runs without landing; headroom below 2.3 m.
metrics.basis: DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2 and s4.3.
metrics.method: Check ramp profiles and soffit heights.

metrics.name: Step-free public entrances
metrics.good: All primary public entrances and the station link step-free from the sidewalk.
metrics.bad: Any public entrance needing a step or a separate back route.
metrics.basis: Vancouver Building By-law Part 3.8 and CSA B651 not opened; target stated as a design intent, to be checked by the code consultant.
metrics.method: Graph routing with step edges removed.

metrics.name: Truncated-dome treatment at flush crossings
metrics.good: Required where grade break between sidewalk and ramp top is under 5%.
metrics.bad: Flush crossing without tactile surface.
metrics.basis: EDM 2026 section 8.4.1.4.
metrics.method: Check each crossing point for grade break and tactile flag.

modules.method: Compute a slope raster from the DEM and site grading, or slope profiles along each route edge from P06-M04. Classify running slope as 0-5% (green), 5-8.3% (amber, ramp) and above 8.3% (red). Measure crossfall from sections. Remove edges with steps from the walk graph to find step-free routes between each public entrance, the sidewalk, the plaza and the station link; report any entrance with no step-free route. Place seating nodes and compute the longest gap along each route against the group distances. Check headroom of canopies and stair undersides, landing intervals on ramps and tactile-dome presence at flush crossings. Compile code-based items for the code consultant (Vancouver Building By-law, CSA B651) as a manual checklist, not a computed result.
visualization: Ground-plane slope map with three classes (green up to 5%, amber 5-8.3%, red above 8.3%), small arrows for direction of fall and a legend in percent and ratio.
Rest-coverage overlay: 50 m, 100 m and 150 m radius rings around seating nodes, shaded by group.
Step-free route traces from each public entrance to the station link, breaks marked with an X and the clause that fails.
Checklist panel with badges linked to EDM and DfT clauses; code items shown as 'needs consultant' chips.
modules.human_judgment: Lived-experience review with the City's disability advisory groups, wayfinding clarity, sensory and cognitive comfort (glare, noise, complexity), dignity of access (no separate back door), and independent accessibility rating such as the Rick Hansen Foundation certification (not opened).
modules.limits: Code compliance cannot be proven from a massing model. Slope needs an elevation model; downtown grade data may need City LiDAR. The DfT and EDM numbers differ on crossfall and the UK standard is an external benchmark. No door, handrail or washroom geometry exists in Layer 0.

modules.name: Vertical public realm: public uses at height
modules.design_question: Do public, cultural and civic uses extend up the tower in a way that is genuinely open, reachable and worth visiting, not just a token lobby or ticketed deck?
modules.effort: About 3-4 person-days; reads program tags per storey, access attributes are manual.
inputs: Layer0.ProgramTags per storey: public | cultural_civic | amenity | retail | hotel | office | residential | mechanical | core
Storey heights and areas from Layer 0 massing; crown height
VerticalCirculation tags: lift banks (public or tenant), escalators, stairs (from advanced presets, or placeholders)
AccessAttributes per public space: free | ticketed | booked, opening hours, covenant yes/no, outdoor or indoor
Terrace and roof polygons flagged public
outputs: VerticalPublicProfile: {storey, height_m, public_gfa_m2, access_regime}[]
PublicShareAboveStreetwall: number (%)
HighestPublicStoreyHeight_m and ratio to total height
MaxGapBetweenPublicLevels: number (storeys and m)
VerticalPublicChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08, SYST for egress, PRES boards)

parameters.name: Public and cultural share of floor area above the streetwall
parameters.relationship: More public floor area above the podium -> stronger sense that public life reaches up the tower; but each public floor needs separate lifts, security and egress and displaces revenue floors.

parameters.name: Height of the highest public storey
parameters.relationship: A public level near the crown gives skyline and mountain views and a reason to travel up; but the top floors are the most valuable and most exposed to wind.

parameters.name: Vertical gap between public levels
parameters.relationship: Large gaps break the idea that public uses extend vertically; sky lobbies and stacked civic rooms at regular intervals make a legible vertical sequence.

parameters.name: Dedicated public vertical circulation
parameters.relationship: Separate public lifts or escalators keep public access independent of tenants and security, but need lobby space and core area; London policy asks for a separate entrance (not opened).

parameters.name: Access regime and hours
parameters.relationship: Free walk-up access and long hours widen the public; booked or ticketed access narrows it. London's Sky Garden is free with a booked ticket and open until midnight; Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre is ticketed.

parameters.name: Size and height of interior public space
parameters.relationship: Rooms at least about 93 m2 and 9.1 m high read as civic spaces; lobbies serving principal entries and circulation do not count as interior public space.

parameters.name: Outdoor public terraces at height
parameters.relationship: Open-air public terraces add views and weather exposure; wind comfort there comes from the CLIM wind module and may limit hours or types of use.

metrics.name: Public or cultural GFA above the streetwall
metrics.good: At least 5% of above-podium GFA (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 1% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy asks that, where possible, a building include community-significant uses such as a public observation deck or other public amenity; no number exists. VTC brief asks that public-facing uses extend vertically.
metrics.method: Sum GFA of public and cultural_civic storeys above the podium line divided by total GFA above it.

metrics.name: Distinct public levels above the podium
metrics.good: At least two separated public levels, one in the top quarter of building height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: No public level above the podium.
metrics.basis: No sourced threshold; the preset follows the brief's vertical continuity intent.
metrics.method: Cluster public storeys; count clusters and note the highest.

metrics.name: Maximum gap between public levels
metrics.good: At most one quarter of total height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: More than one half of total height (editable preset).
metrics.basis: Placeholder; no sourced rule.
metrics.method: Difference between consecutive public storey heights, plus ground to first and last to roof.

metrics.name: Interior public space quality floor
metrics.good: At least about 93.0 m2 and about 9.1 m clear height, secured by covenant.
metrics.bad: Smaller or lower, or secured only by lease; lobbies for principal entries and circulation are excluded.
metrics.basis: CDDG S3.3.1 and glossary 'interior public space' (applies for floor-area exclusions; used here as a quality floor).
metrics.method: Check area and floor-to-ceiling height of tagged public rooms.

metrics.name: Public access hours and cost at height
metrics.good: Free, open to the public from at least 10:00 to 22:00, seven days (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Office hours only, ticketed, or by invitation.
metrics.basis: Sky Garden London is free with booking and opens to midnight (precedent); Vancouver Lookout is ticketed. The City memo of April 2026 treats ticketed Lookout access as typical. The 2002 staff report judged a hotel lobby plus roof garden an inadequate public amenity.
metrics.method: Read access attributes per public node.

metrics.name: Public vertical circulation
metrics.good: Dedicated public lifts or an independent public lobby with its own entrance (preset).
metrics.bad: Public level reached only via tenant lobby.
metrics.basis: Based on London Plan Policy D9 intent, which was not opened (Cloudflare challenge).
metrics.method: Check circulation tags for separation.

modules.method: Read the storey table from Layer 0 and tag each storey by public, cultural or civic programme and area. Identify the podium line from the first tower step-back (shared with P06-M02). Compute public share of floor area above the podium, number and positions of public clusters, vertical gaps, height of the highest public storey, and area and clear height of each interior public room. Read access attributes (free, ticketed, hours, covenant) from each public node, and the vertical circulation tags to test separation from tenant lifts. Compare with threshold table and mark each result verified, team assumption or unverified. Pass public occupant demand to the SYST (egress) and MOBI (lift capacity) packets.
visualization: Vertical strip diagram: tower elevation as a column from 0 to total height in metres, one band per storey coloured by programme, public storeys outlined with a heavy stroke, lift lines drawn, markers at the highest public storey and the podium line.
Per-node 24-hour clock-arc showing opening hours and a chip for free, booked or ticketed.
Histogram of public GFA per 10-storey band; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG S3.3.1 and the preset table.
modules.human_judgment: Whether the space is welcoming rather than token, programme curation and cultural content (including Indigenous perspectives), cost and security screening, equity of access, management, and safety and egress for large public loads at height.
modules.limits: Threshold presets have no sourced value; only the interior-room floor (from CDDG) and precedents are cited. Life-safety, lift capacity and wind comfort at height belong to other packets. Access regime is user-entered, not computed. CTBUH material was not opened (403).

modules.name: Gehl-type public-life scorecard: what can be computed and what needs people
modules.design_question: Which of Gehl's twelve public-space quality criteria can the tool compute from the massing, which only through proxies, and which need human audit or field observation?
modules.effort: About 4-6 person-days for the triage matrix, radar and manual audit form; agent-based public-life prediction is roadmap.
inputs: Check outputs of P06-M01 to P06-M07
CLIM: sun, wind, rain-shelter and noise results (if available)
ECOL: tree canopy and planting (if available)
Manual audit form (microscale streetscape audit items) filled by team members
Optional baseline: public-life counts of the existing site (Gehl-style stationary activity and movement counts)
outputs: CriteriaTriage: {criterion, group, mode: computed | proxy | human | field, value, confidence}[12]
PublicLifeProfile: radar data with computed and judged axes distinguished
PlaceDiagramMap: mapping of results to four place qualities
Gaps: list of criteria still without evidence (for the policy reflection board)

parameters.name: Criterion weights (editable)
parameters.relationship: Weights set how much each criterion counts in any summary view; the jury weights human-scale experience at 40%, but no validated weighting between criteria exists, so a single composite is discouraged.

parameters.name: Evidence mode per criterion
parameters.relationship: A criterion moves from 'human' to 'proxy' to 'computed' as the tool gains data; shows what remains judgment and keeps the scorecard honest.

parameters.name: Audit item set (microscale audit)
parameters.relationship: Structured audit items (for example MAPS-Global) make human ratings repeatable between raters; reported inter-rater reliability was mostly 'excellent' in a Japanese online-audit study.

parameters.name: Baseline public-life counts
parameters.relationship: Counts of people moving and staying before and after a design show real effect; they cannot come from a massing model and are post-occupancy or existing-site work.

metrics.name: Protection against traffic and accidents
metrics.good: Fed by vehicle crossings, crossing distances, and sidewalk width (P06-M01, P06-M05); needs street data for speeds.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Gehl twelve criteria, recalled from Cities for People (not opened). Triage: proxy.
metrics.method: Weighted proxy from P06-M01 service crossings and P06-M05 comfort.

metrics.name: Protection against crime and violence (eyes on the street)
metrics.good: Proxy from active frontage, transparency, night-time uses and absence of long blank runs; lighting needs human input.
metrics.bad: Long blank runs and no night uses.
metrics.basis: Triage: proxy. CDDG supports passive security by lighting, transparency and activity (G3.1.1).
metrics.method: Combine P06-M01 outputs with manual lighting rating.

metrics.name: Protection against unpleasant sensory experiences (wind, rain, noise, pollution)
metrics.good: Wind and shelter computed from CLIM and weather protection (P06-M01); noise and air need other models.
metrics.bad: Strolling-class wind at seating or no weather protection.
metrics.basis: Triage: computed for wind, shelter; other items need other packets.
metrics.method: Pull P06-M01 weather-protection coverage and CLIM wind classes.

metrics.name: Opportunities to walk and to stand or stay
metrics.good: Computed clear widths, slopes, edge articulation and plaza edges (P06-M02, M05, M06); quality of edge zone needs human rating.
metrics.bad: Clear width below standard or no edge zones.
metrics.basis: Triage: computed plus human.
metrics.method: Aggregate P06-M05 and P06-M06 checks; manual edge-zone rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to sit and to see
metrics.good: Seating supply and sun (P06-M03) computed; view distance and sightlines can be computed by isovist; seat quality and interest of views are human.
metrics.bad: No seating or no sun on seating.
metrics.basis: Triage: computed plus human.
metrics.method: P06-M03 results plus optional isovist.

metrics.name: Opportunities to hear and talk; play and exercise
metrics.good: Noise needs an acoustic model; play and exercise are programme and human judgments.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: Triage: human or field.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries.

metrics.name: Scale (human scale)
metrics.good: Podium proportion, unit rhythm and massing variation computed (P06-M01, P06-M02); perception needs human check.
metrics.bad: Podium outside the band or unit frontage beyond range.
metrics.basis: Thresholds from CDDG via P06-M01 and P06-M02.
metrics.method: Aggregate P06-M01 and P06-M02 check results.

metrics.name: Positive aspects of climate; positive sensory experiences
metrics.good: Sun hours and shelter computed (P06-M03, M01); trees from ECOL; materials, detailing and views are human judgments.
metrics.bad: Shaded, windy plaza with no planting.
metrics.basis: Triage: computed plus human.
metrics.method: P06-M03 sun hours, ECOL canopy, manual rating.

metrics.name: Share of criteria with computed or proxy evidence
metrics.good: Reported as a count out of 12; target is to move criteria from 'human' to 'proxy' over time (preset: at least 6 of 12 by 10 Dec 2026).
metrics.bad: Fewer than 4 of 12.
metrics.basis: Project management measure, not a design threshold.
metrics.method: Count criteria whose mode is computed or proxy.

modules.method: Create a 12-row triage matrix, one row per Gehl criterion, grouped into protection (traffic, crime, unpleasant experiences), comfort (walk, stand, sit, see, hear/talk, play) and delight (scale, climate, sensory). For each row record the evidence mode (computed, proxy, human audit, field observation) and link the module outputs used. Pull verified checks from P06-M01 to P06-M07 and show their source badges. For human rows, present a short audit form based on a microscale streetscape audit and record rater initials and date. Show the radar with computed axes drawn solid and judged axes hatched. Provide a cross-map to the four-quality Place Diagram (access, activities, comfort and image, sociability). Never output a single composite score; show profile and gaps.
visualization: Twelve-axis radar in three colour groups (protection, comfort, delight); computed axes solid fill, proxy axes dotted outline, human-only axes hatched, field-only axes empty with a dashed ring.
Triage matrix: rows are criteria, columns are computed / proxy / human audit / field data, with the source module and clause linked in each cell.
Four-quadrant Place Diagram overlay (access and linkages, uses and activities, comfort and image, sociability) with counts of evidence per quadrant.
Badge 'Human-scale experience: 40% of jury' on the profile; FALSE ASSUMPTION colour for any retracted rating.
modules.human_judgment: Almost all 'delight' criteria, edge quality, seat comfort, perceived safety, noise tolerance, cultural meaning and inclusion. Field counts and surveys can only be done on a built or existing place. The scorecard exists to mark that boundary.
modules.limits: Gehl's criteria wording and any quantity (for example door counts per 100 m or viewing distances) were recalled, not opened, so no Gehl numbers are used as thresholds. No validated composite exists. Proxies measure the model, not behaviour; counts of people need field work.

R1: Built sun metrics on the Downtown Peninsula solar guidelines (22 Sep, 10:00-16:00, 15-minute steps, coverage formula) and amended PDT to PT wording.

notes: Process notes. (1) The shared web-search budget ran out after the first calls, so most evidence comes from direct reads of City of Vancouver documents (Council report PDFs and the Engineering Design Manual, read as text in the browser pane), TfL, UK DfT, NYC zoning, PubMed abstracts and repository pages. (2) Pages on guidelines.vancouver.ca and bylaws.vancouver.ca refused automated access; one download was triggered and not retried. Nothing was saved or downloaded by us except two PDFs that the fetch tool stored automatically (TfL, DfT) and which were read locally. (3) The London Plan site showed a bot challenge and was not bypassed. (4) PubMed sources require attribution: 'According to PubMed' with DOI links (given in S24 and S25). (5) Licence cautions for an open-source tool: Ladybug is AGPL-3.0 and depthmapX is GPL-3.0 (strong copyleft); JuPedSim and IfcOpenShell are LGPL-3.0; City open data needs the Open Government Licence - Vancouver attribution line. (6) CDDG numbers are guidelines ('typically', 'generally'), not by-law limits; the brief says the jury may reward justified breaches, so the tool should show a breach with its source clause and a free-text justification rather than a hard fail. (7) VTC block area 79.2 m x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2 was calculated by us; 10% = about 1,147 m2 and 20% = about 2,294 m2. (8) Priority: core (course working core 13 Nov or VTC entrants before 30 Nov) = M01, M02, M03, M04, M07; v1 (by 10 Dec) = M05, M06, M08.
